title: Methods
bridge: Methods declare return and parameter types: `static double Area(double w, double h) => w * h;` (the `=>` form is for one-liners). Optional parameters: `double Total(int qty, double price, double discount = 0)`. Overloading works as in Java.

exercises.title: Temperatures
exercises.prompt: Write CToF(double c) and FToC(double f) in class Temps, rounded to 1 decimal.
hints: public static double CToF(double c) => Math.Round(c * 9 / 5 + 32, 1);

exercises.title: Optional discount
exercises.prompt: Write Total(int qty, double unitPrice, double discountPercent = 0) in class Price: rounded to 2 decimals; throw ArgumentException if the discount isn't 0-100.
hints: The default value goes in the parameter list: double discountPercent = 0
if (discountPercent < 0 || discountPercent > 100) throw new ArgumentException("bad discount");

quiz.q: double Total(int q, double p, double d = 0) can be called as…
What does => do in static int Twice(int x) => x * 2;?

cards.a: double d = 0 in the parameter list
out parameters, e.g. TryParse(text, out int n)

explain: Explain methods to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up.
